editorial_reason: ProofWiki explicitly records both zero-including and zero-excluding conventions, then a separate Peano axiomatization. For integer construction, N includes 0 so [a,b] may model negative, zero and positive differences; no claim is made that a concrete set of von Neumann ordinals is literally identical to every Peano model. The Peano axioms are an alternative axiomatic characterization, not interchangeable set-theoretic underlying objects.

ProofWiki Definition 1 gives the three exact conditions. The Stacks Project similarly treats relations on a set as subsets of S×S and equivalence as reflexive symmetric transitive; geometric equivalence relations of schemes are a distinct context and must not replace this one. The integer pairs construction uses an equivalence relation on N×N, which is mathematically separate from the sequence-equivalence relation used to construct real numbers.

Source defines the class as the subset of S containing all elements equivalent to x and identifies representatives. Since ∼ is symmetric, {y:y∼x} and {y:x∼y} are equal. The class is a subset of S, not the singleton {x} unless all equivalence classes are singletons. This class precedes the quotient S/∼ and provides the element construction for integers.

ProofWiki defines the quotient precisely as the set of equivalence classes under a specified relation. The canonical quotient map x↦[x] is a separately defined function and the universal factorization property is a theorem, not an additional quotient-set definition. Care is required not to confuse the underlying quotient set with a quotient ring/group which requires compatible operations.
